criteria.notes: Split verdict, and the split is why this box stays unticked. CLAUSE ONE ("a run completes only when every requirement's EvidenceRecord carries a confirmed remote revision") is evidenced end-to-end and non-vacuously — the negative half (`allGatesPassed` false while req2 is unbound) and the positive half are both asserted, and the third requirement in the fixture tracks nothing remote and passes trivially, so a gate that blocked everything would not satisfy it. CLAUSE TWO is not. The criterion says the edit "halts the run via 11's `material amendment` stop condition"; what the suite proves is that a phase-21 signal, handed to a phase-21 `throwIfMaterialAmendment` that the test's own helper invokes two lines before the gate call, throws. 11's actual stop condition (`haltOnStopCondition`, kind `material_amendment`, which transitions the run to `blocked` and journals an `adjudication_decision`) is never reached and is not imported on this path, and has **no production caller** anywhere — its only four call sites are its own unit test and `packages/cli/src/intake/intake.e2e.test.ts:232`, and none is in or reachable from `packages/gates`. CORRECTION, 2026-08-02, review of PR #76: an earlier draft of this record said "no caller anywhere in the repository", which is false — the grep behind it excluded `*.test.*` and so did not reproduce. The narrower statement is the true one and is what the UNMET verdict rests on; the reviewer confirmed the verdict is unaffected, since `gates` has no `supervisor` dependency and no production code consumes `MaterialAmendmentSignal`. The distinction matters in the useful direction too: 11's halt is *tested* end-to-end for all seven kinds including `material_amendment`, so what is missing is the wiring, not the mechanism. The roadmap's own §In scope predicts the path "reached transitively via 14→13→11"; that path does not exist at 30f931e. Substituting a phase-21-local throw for phase 11's stop condition is a WEAKER guarantee, not a more precise description of the same one, so the wording protocol does not apply (brief RULING: "A weaker guarantee is never a wording fix — it is UNMET"). SECOND, INDEPENDENT GAP on this criterion's own named evidence: it asks for "the halted run's journal excerpt". The halt path journals nothing — it throws before `registry.fireByTag` is called, and the only journal-query assertions in the suite (:148-166) belong to the run that COMPLETES. `docs/evidence/phase-21/README.md`'s "Journal excerpt (MAJOR-1's named evidence artifact)" section presents entries from that completing scenario (req2 blocked-then-passed) under a heading that reads as the halted run's excerpt; quoting the transcript rather than the README's summary of it is what surfaced this. Both gaps and the smallest honest remedy are in the defect record.

criteria.notes: Two precisions that narrow what this tick means; neither is a hedge, both are checkable. (a) THE TRANSITION BOUNDARY. `final_verifying` is a caller-supplied `GateContext` field on this path, not an enforced one: `packages/gates/src/registry.ts`'s `fireByTag`/`fireAll` never inspect `context.stage` and `EvidenceRecordSchema` has no stage member, so the cited tests would read identically with `stage: "verifying"`. Nothing in the shipped product fires `remote_verification` at the `final_verifying`→`published_local` edge — `createRemoteVerificationGate` has zero non-test callers, and `fireFinalCandidateVerification` (`final-candidate.ts:45-47`, the one function that does enforce the stage) is likewise test-only. What this box evidences is the gate's verdict: a `unsupported`/`ambiguous_write` outcome yields `passed: false`, which makes `allGatesPassed` false, which is the condition final-candidate re-verification consults. The same narrowing is already on record for the sibling perf gate — `docs/evidence/criteria-closeout/phase-15.json` criterion 5's notes, and `docs/interface-ledger.md` Gap 21 ('createPerformanceGateHandler still has no production caller'). This record does not claim shipped enforcement. (b) WHERE "ACTIONABLE" LIVES. The canonical kind is in `GateVerdict.detail` ('blocked: remote operation resolved to canonical "unsupported" — never a silent pass'), and `EvidenceRecordSchema` is `.strict()` with no `detail` field, so the journaled record carries `command: "remote_verification"`, `exitStatus: 1`, `gateVerdict: "failed"` and `gateTag` — enough to identify the failing gate and rule out a silent pass, not enough to name which of the two canonical kinds fired. The criterion's own channel is the fault-matrix test, which asserts the detail directly.

criteria.notes: PRODUCED, NOT REINTERPRETED. Before this pass `drift-ci.yml` had exactly one recorded run — 30256034367, scheduled, green — so the criterion's "red CI check" half had no evidence at all, and per the brief's RULING 1 a green run plus a local transcript would have been a channel downgrade rather than a closeout. The red half was producible without a code change, using the workflow's own documented `workflow_dispatch` drift-simulation inputs, so it was produced: three dispatches at main `30f931ea`, no scratch branch and no repository change. WHAT WAS BUMPED. The pinned fixture (`pinned-fixtures.ts`, `PINNED_JIRA_VERSION = "1000.0.0"`) is untouched — bumping it would violate the criterion's own "zero pinned-fixture changes" clause — and the OBSERVED half is overridden to 1001.0.0, which is exactly the comparison `compareDriftFixture` makes (`snapshot.pinnedVersion !== snapshot.observedVersion`). That exercises the version-drift limb only; the shape-drift limb (a withdrawn `description` field, the roadmap test plan's own example) has no `workflow_dispatch` input and is evidenced by the unit citation above. DEFECT FOUND WHILE PRODUCING THIS. The first red attempt (run 30743929773) emitted TWO proposals, not one, because `cli.ts:143` tests `process.env["GRAFANA_OBSERVED_VERSION"] !== undefined` and an unsupplied `workflow_dispatch` string input arrives as the empty string, not as absent — so the un-bumped connector was compared against an observed version of "". The same is true on the `schedule` trigger, where `${{ inputs.* }}` is likewise blank: the one historical scheduled run (30256034367) shows '  JIRA_OBSERVED_VERSION: ' and '  GRAFANA_OBSERVED_VERSION: ' blank in its own job log, and stayed green only because it was the first sample under a threshold-2 debounce. Filed as `docs/evidence/criteria-closeout/defects/21-drift-ci-blank-dispatch-input-false-positive.md`. It does not undermine this tick — the cited red run supplies both inputs explicitly and produces exactly one proposal — but a reader must know the scheduled job's steady state is a two-connector false positive. Not fixed here: verify-your-own-fix is self-review. LIVE SCOPE, unchanged by this pass: the "observed" half is fixture/env-modeled, never a live Jira or Grafana probe, exactly as `docs/evidence/phase-21/README.md` and the roadmap's §Risks note already disclose.

criteria.notes: Five of the seven manifest entries do what the criterion says. `jira-forged-admin-delete` calls 18's real `assertAllowedJiraOperation`; `jira-redaction` calls 18's real `containsSecretShapedContent` against a real `ConnectorError.toData()`; `grafana-redaction` calls 20's real `redactSecretBearingObject`; `gateway-redaction` calls 16's real `mapHttpStatusToConnectorError`; `grafana-forged-admin-delete` constructs a real `createGrafanaProviderAdapter` and inspects its surface (a re-implementation of 20's `forgedDeleteAdminScenario` that drops that scenario's `calls.length === 0` half, but still exercises 20's real constructor). The two TENANT-BOUNDARY entries do not. Both call `assertTenantBoundary("tenant-a", "tenant-b")` — this phase's own three-line string comparison, on two literals — so both verdicts are constants that no change anywhere in `packages/connectors-jira` or `packages/connectors-grafana` can flip. That is the brief's can-never-fail vacuity pattern in its purer form: not a type mismatch, but a fixture that never sets up the state the assertion describes, so no tenant boundary is ever crossed. The criterion's whole point (roadmap §In scope: these fixtures are "registered as standing, blocking entries ... rather than one-off phase-exit tests", "proof that these fixtures graduated") is defeated for that category: 20's genuine `tenantBoundaryBreachScenario` remains a one-off phase-exit test, and the standing gate that replaced it is inert. `docs/evidence/phase-21/README.md` Deviation 4 discloses the substitution and justifies it as "neither connector package exported a dedicated tenant-boundary assertion function of its own prior to this phase" — true of an *assertion function*, and beside the point, because 20 exported a self-verifying *scenario* addressed to this phase by name. Ticking this would assert something factually wrong about the system for two of seven entries and would lose a real guarantee, so the wording protocol does not apply. THE ANTI-VACUITY CHECK, done by reading both operands rather than trusting the matcher: these are two string arrays over an overlapping vocabulary, and they DO intersect on the member spelled blocked, so the filtered intersection built at remote-verification-gate.test.ts line 139 is non-empty. The negated containment assertions therefore run against a genuinely populated intersection and are not a category error that cannot fail.

the verbose reporter names this exact case on its own line — 'src/remote-verification-gate.test.ts > enum-disjointness' and, on the same line, 'never on final_verifying/published_local/done 14ms' — in a run summarised ' Test Files  2 passed (2)' / '      Tests  21 passed (21)'. criteria.notes: The `blocked` overlap is real and is not a hole in the tick: the criterion names three strings (`done`, `final_verifying`, `published_local`) and the test disproves membership for exactly those three, in both directions, against the live imported constants. 18's own `workflow-stage.ts` documents the `blocked` coincidence separately as "same spelling, unrelated enum". Because both unions are `as const` arrays imported from their owning packages, a future edit that added `done` to the run lifecycle, or `published_local` to the Jira stage set, would turn this test red without anyone touching it — which is what makes it a proof rather than a restatement.
